transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Dale Willman.
A federal appeals court has rejected the Justice Department's request to set aside
thousands of California ballots, NPR's Drew Joffe-Black reports.
In a two-to-one vote, a Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals panel rejected the
Trump administration's request.
The Justice Department wants California election officials to stop processing
ballots pertaining to 20,000 people, federal officials say are likely
non-citizens.
But the accuracy of that list is in question.
The appeals court ruling upholds a federal court opinion from earlier this week.
The majority noted the Justice Department's last-minute request could
disenfranchise eligible voters and put the vote-counting process in jeopardy.
The same two judges had already ruled against the Justice Department earlier
in this case.
A third judge dissented. Drew Joffe-Black, NPR News.
President Trump won Michigan in 2024.
Now Democrats there are trying to hang on to an open seat.
NPR's Sam Greenglass reports.
Democrats here nominated former public health official Abdul El-Sayed,
testing how a Democrat from the party's left flank will fair in a purple state.
Former Congressman Mike Rogers is the Republican nominee, and his closing
message has focused on painting El-Sayed as dangerous, accusing him without
evidence of ties to terrorist groups.
My whole family wore the uniform in the United States of America
so we could pray any way that we wanted.
It's not how he prays, it's how he thinks.
El-Sayed has disputed the claims he would be the first Muslim American
in the Senate and says Republicans are trying to distract voters.
Me and my name and my faith are not the reason you can't see a doctor.
Not the reason you can't afford your gas.
Not the reason that you can't afford your groceries.
The race is considered a toss-up.
Sam Greenglass, NPR News, in Hanover and Wyandotte, Michigan.
A federal judge says he'll be extremely frustrated if the Department of Justice
arrests former FBI Director James Comey while he's weighing arguments to dismiss the case.
Comey's lawyers say the DOJ is out of time to bring any charges.
NPR's Kerry Johnson has more on our reports.
Lawyers for Jim Comey say prosecutors had 10 years to indict him
on allegations of leaking national security information in 2016.
They say that time has now come to an end
and the judge should shut the door once and for all.
Comey's lawyers say he still faces possible arrest by the bureau he once led,
which has had FBI agents stationed outside his home.
Judge Trevor McFadden told prosecutors not to conduct an early morning search,
but the judge seemed inclined to give prosecutors a bit more time
to convince a grand jury to indict Comey.
Prosecutors say they're presenting new evidence,
including an allegation from 2017 that could extend the statute of limitations.
Comey denies any wrongdoing.
Kerry Johnson, NPR News.
Stocks close down across the board on Wall Street today
and you're listening to NPR News.
Evacuations from the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky began on Friday,
about 2,000 residents remain there,
and they've been given a choice of leaving for either Ukraine
or Russia-held territory.
The evacuations began on the fourth day of a localized truce.
Fighting, however, continued elsewhere.
A Russian drone strike in northeast Ukraine killed at least one person
and injured eight others.
Astronomers appear to have tracked down new x-ray sources
that are decidedly Halloween-themed.
Reporter Ari Daniel Dazmore.
Studying x-rays offers a window into the dynamics of extreme cosmic phenomena.
Researchers looking back at data collected by NASA's Chandra telescope
were stunned to find 84 new sources of the very lowest energy x-rays
spread across half a dozen galaxies.
It's likely they're produced by systems involving something super dense
like a black hole that's stealing material off a nearby star.
Like a vampire, says University of Alabama astronomer Jimmy Irwin.
Instead of stealing blood, they're stealing material from a companion star.
Another possible source could be two black holes orbiting one another,
pulling matter off a star,
a situation that yields a kind of donut-shaped void called a zombie disk.
For NPR News, I'm Ari Daniel.
Police in Milwaukee say as many as 750,000 people turned out Friday
to celebrate the first-ever World Series title for the Milwaukee Brewers.
Fans flooded the streets, cheered from office-building windows,
and gathered at a downtown amphitheater to welcome the team home
after they beat the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 on Wednesday.
I'm Dale Willman, NPR News in Cleveland.

topics.text: Ninth Circuit panel rejects Justice Department bid to set aside 20,000 California ballots
Michigan Senate race: Abdul El-Sayed and Mike Rogers in toss-up contest for open seat
Judge warns DOJ against arresting James Comey while weighing statute of limitations dismissal
Russian-occupied Oleshky evacuations begin during localized truce; about 2,000 residents remain
Astronomers find 84 new low-energy X-ray sources in six galaxies, possibly black holes
Milwaukee crowds of up to 750,000 celebrate Brewers' first World Series title
